To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the sectoral distribution of FDI is largely driven by the sectoral composition of the economy and by the relative importance of capital costs in each sector.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the sectoral distribution of FDI flows in Poland and the factors that explain the patterns observed.
the sectoral patterns of FDI and the determinants of these patterns in a country undergoing economic transition.
the determinants of sectoral patterns in FDI in transition countries.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in general, the FDI patterns in the manufacturing sector of Poland reflect the same determinants as in developed countries, but that the effects of the determinants are more pronounced and that the effects are not equally distributed across industries.
the sectoral patterns of FDI are influenced by the same general factors as in other countries.
FDI is attracted to countries and industries where it can earn a higher rate of return than in other countries and sectors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the case of Poland, the determinants of foreign investment flows vary considerably across manufacturing industries.
the sectoral patterns of FDI in Poland are consistent with the notion of FDI as a substitute for trade.
, in the Polish case, FDI has been a major force for the development of the country's economy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in addition to the usual gravity factors (such as market size, distance, and language), the industry-specific characteristics of the host country are important for FDI.
the sectoral patterns of foreign investment in Poland have been shaped by the country’s economic transition and the resulting changes in the structure of its economy.
the sectoral patterns of FDI flows in the early stages of transition are likely to differ from those in mature economies.
